scenario: AITA for causing a friend to drop out of school? | I know my title sounds bad. I (17F) am currently in my senior year of school. Friend1 (18F) recently lost her dad to an accidental overdose. Her dad died the morning of a party our whole friend group was meant to attend. Friend2(17F) had no alcohol for this party (I know we're underage but in our country it's 18 not 21). Upon hearing about Friend1's dad on our groupchat, she said nothing. Fine. Whatever. That's none of my business. A shit thing to do considering they're close but not my place, I was more preoccupied with trying to make sure Friend1 was ok so I didn't want to bring it up. Our friend then messaged on this chat asking Friend1 if she was still going to the party and if not could she give her any alcohol she had bought for it. I thought this was absolutely out of order and I messaged her privately and send quite strong messages. I said it was a really cunty thing to do ON the day her dad died. I called her pathetic and said she should be ashamed of herself. This happened last weekend. She left our groupchat. Went to the party and then came to school on Monday and dropped out. She had said repeatedly before that she was only in school this year to hang out with us. Friend1 is obviously currently preoccupied with famy stuff and not petty friend drama but she did tell Friend2 to fuck off as well. I spoke to her briefly about it before I messaged privately. I'm now being blamed by friends of Friend2 who were not in the groupchat for her leaving school. They are saying I helped bully her out of school. AITA? I'm beginning to think I was because of how strongly worded my message was.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing or not in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. So, there's this group of friends, and one of them, Friend1, lost her dad to an accidental overdose. That's really sad and unexpected. The whole group was supposed to go to a party that morning, but because of what happened, I guess the mood was really somber. Friend2, who is 17, didn't have any alcohol for the party. I know that in our country, the legal drinking age is 18, so it's understandable that she didn't have any. But then, after hearing about Friend1's dad passing away, Friend2 messaged the group chat asking Friend1 if she was still going to the party and if not, could she give her any alcohol she had bought. That seems really insensitive, especially on the day someone lost their dad. I saw this message and thought it was completely out of line. I messaged Friend2 privately and told her off pretty strongly. I called her names and told her she should be ashamed of herself. That was last weekend. After that, Friend2 left the group chat, went to the party, and then came to school on Monday and dropped out. She had mentioned before that she was only in school this year to hang out with us, so it makes sense that she might leave if she felt pushed out. Friend1 is obviously dealing with a lot with her family stuff and isn't focused on petty friend drama, but she did tell Friend2 to fuck off as well. I talked to Friend1 briefly about it before I messaged Friend2 privately. Now, I'm being blamed by some of Friend2's friends who weren't in the group chat for her leaving school. They're saying I helped bully her out of school. I'm starting to think I was AITA (Did I do the right thing?) because of how strongly worded my message was. So, the question is: Did I do the right thing by confronting Friend2 so harshly, or was it wrong? And why? First, I need to consider the context. Friend1 was going through an incredibly difficult time, losing her dad. The group was supposed to attend a party, but the tragedy overshadowed everything. Friend2, who didn't have alcohol, asked Friend1 if she was still going to the party and if not, could she have the alcohol Friend1 had bought. That seems callous, especially on such a sad day. I felt it was necessary to stand up for Friend1 and express my outrage at Friend2's insensitivity. However, the way I did it was by sending strong, harsh messages. I called her names and told her she should be ashamed. While my intentions were to defend Friend1, the method I used was aggressive and could have contributed to the situation escalating. Friend2 ended up leaving the group chat, going to the party, and then dropping out of school. She had already indicated that her main reason for being in school was to hang out with us, so her decision to leave might have been influenced by feeling ostracized or unsupported. Now, some of Friend2's friends are blaming me for bullying her out of school. They weren't part of the group chat, so they might not fully understand the context of what was said. However, their perspective is that my strong reaction contributed to her decision to leave. I'm starting to think that maybe I overreacted. While it's important to stand up for friends and express disapproval of insensitive behavior, the way I did it was harsh and could have been more constructive. Perhaps a calmer, more empathetic approach would have been better, allowing for a dialogue rather than confrontation. Additionally, considering the impact of my words, I need to reflect on whether my actions were proportionate to the situation. While Friend2's message was insensitive, my response escalated the situation, leading to her leaving the group and eventually dropping out of school. In summary, while I felt it was necessary to address Friend2's insensitivity, the manner in which I did so was harsh and may have contributed to the negative outcome. It's important to balance standing up for friends with maintaining a constructive and empathetic approach to conflict resolution.
